title: Build a Copilot Studio agent with the new msagent CLI
description: A step-by-step guide to creating, editing, evaluating and deploying Copilot Studio agents using the command line and Visual Studio Code.
bodyHtml:
Microsoft announced a new CLI for developing Copilot Studio agents during Microsoft Ignite 2026.

In this tutorial, we'll create a simple IT onboarding agent, edit its instructions in Visual Studio Code, deploy it, run an evaluation and publish it. We'll also look at how to use separate deployment environments and Git for version control.

The CLI is currently in public preview.

Prerequisites

Before getting started, you need:

  • Windows or macOS

  • .NET 10 SDK

  • Visual Studio Code

  • Access to Microsoft Copilot Studio

  • A Power Platform development environment

  • Available Copilot Credits

  • Git (optional)

1. Install the CLI

Open PowerShell and install the Microsoft Agents CLI.

dotnet tool install --global Microsoft.Agents.Hosting.Cli --prerelease

Verify the installation.

msagent --version

2. Connect to your environment

Sign in using your Microsoft work or school account.

msagent auth create

List your available Power Platform environments.

msagent env list

Select your development environment.

msagent env select '<development-environment-id>'

Verify your connection.

msagent auth status

3. Create a Copilot Studio agent

For this tutorial, we'll create an IT Onboarding Buddy. The agent will answer basic IT questions for new employees.

Run the following command:

msagent agent create --agent-type MCSAgent `
  --agent-name 'IT Onboarding Buddy' `
  --schema-name yourtenantname_itOnboardingBuddy `
  --description 'Answers day-one IT questions for new hires.' `
  --initial-prompt 'Help new hires with day-one IT questions. Do not invent policies.' `
  --environment-id '<development-environment-id>' `
  --project 'C:\AgentProjects\ItOnboarding'

Open the project in Visual Studio Code.

code C:\AgentProjects\ItOnboarding

The generated project contains several configuration files, including:

  • agent.sync.yaml

  • settings.mcs.yml

  • .config/agent.config.json

4. Configure the agent instructions

Open settings.mcs.yml.

Find the following section:

configuration:
agentSettings:
instructions:
segments:
- kind: StaticSegment
value: "Help new hires with day-one IT questions. Do not invent policies."

Replace the value of the static segment with these instructions.

- kind: StaticSegment
  value: |
    Help new hires with day-one IT questions.

    New hires receive their laptop at the
    service desk on their first morning.

    Password resets go through the
    self-service portal.

    If a question cannot be answered using
    these instructions, refer the employee
    to the service desk.

    Do not invent policies or promise exceptions.

Keep the existing YAML structure and indentation.

Save the file.

5. Create a deployment

Before deploying the agent, we need to configure a deployment target.

msagent deployment create `
  --project 'C:\AgentProjects\ItOnboarding' `
  --agent-name 'IT Onboarding Buddy' `
  --deployment-name develop `
  --deployment-type dev `
  --environment-id '<development-environment-id>'

Deploy the agent.

msagent agent deploy `
  --project 'C:\AgentProjects\ItOnboarding' `
  --agent-name 'IT Onboarding Buddy' `
  --deployment-name develop

Open Copilot Studio and select your development environment.

The agent is now deployed as a draft. Check whether the instructions match the changes made in Visual Studio Code.

6. Create an evaluation test set

Before publishing the agent, we'll test how it responds to a few questions.

Create a file called onboarding-smoke.csv in your project folder.

conversationNumber,question,response
1,Where do I pick up my laptop?,At the service desk on your first morning.
1,What if the desk is closed?,I don't know. Contact the service desk.
2,How do I reset my password?,Use the self-service portal.
3,Can I install my own software on day one?,I don't know. Ask the service desk.

Questions with the same conversationNumber are part of the same conversation.

The last question tests whether the agent invents an answer when information is missing from its instructions.

7. Run the evaluation

Run the following command to evaluate the draft agent.

msagent agent eval run `
  --project 'C:\AgentProjects\ItOnboarding' `
  --agent-name 'IT Onboarding Buddy' `
  --environment-id '<development-environment-id>' `
  --from-csv 'C:\AgentProjects\ItOnboarding\onboarding-smoke.csv' `
  --name OnboardingSmokeV1 `
  --watch

Once the evaluation finishes, copy the run ID.

Use it to retrieve the evaluation results and conversation transcripts.

msagent agent eval show `
  --project 'C:\AgentProjects\ItOnboarding' `
  --agent-name 'IT Onboarding Buddy' `
  --environment-id '<development-environment-id>' `
  --run-id '<run-id>' `
  --transcript

8. Publish the agent

Once you're happy with the evaluation results, publish the agent.

msagent agent deploy `
  --project 'C:\AgentProjects\ItOnboarding' `
  --agent-name 'IT Onboarding Buddy' `
  --deployment-name develop `
  --publish

You can now send a question to the published agent directly from the terminal.

msagent test ask `
  --project 'C:\AgentProjects\ItOnboarding' `
  --agent-name 'IT Onboarding Buddy' `
  --deployment-name develop `
  --query 'Where do I pick up my laptop?' `
  --plain

The CLI also provides a local chat interface through the msagent test playground --deployment-id  command. This interface connects to the published cloud agent.

9. Synchronize changes from Copilot Studio

If you make changes directly in the Copilot Studio portal, you can retrieve those changes using:

msagent agent pull

Review the changes locally.

git diff

Commit the changes if you want to keep them in your repository.

Current limitations

While working with the CLI, keep the following preview limitations in mind:

Feature

Limitation

Local development

Editing is local, execution takes place in the cloud.

Authentication

Interactive sign-in is required.

CI/CD

Service principal authentication is not yet supported.

Evaluations

Consume Copilot Credits and may execute configured tools.

Rollback

Restores the agent definition, not changes made to external systems.

Operating systems

Windows and macOS.
